excluded: Detailed age structure and cohort dynamics
Political shocks, conflict, pandemics, and climate disasters
included: Population stock and demographic flows of births and deaths
Fertility influences from education and family planning access
Mortality influences from healthcare access and economic resources per capita
Resource pressure created by population growth
boundary_conditions.summary: Model focuses on long-term population change in a developing country driven by births, deaths, education, healthcare, and resource pressure.

dynamic_hypotheses.hypothesis: If fertility remains high, population will grow exponentially until mortality or resource constraints become stronger.
If education and family planning access improve steadily, fertility will decline after a delay, slowing population growth over the long term.
If population grows faster than economic resources, resources per capita will fall, reducing healthcare access and increasing deaths, which counteracts further population growth.

loops.explanation: More population leads to more births, and more births further increase population.
loops.name: Population Growth Through Births

loops.explanation: Population growth reduces resources per capita, which weakens healthcare access, increases mortality and deaths, and thereby slows or reduces population growth.
loops.name: Resource-Constrained Mortality Adjustment

relationships.explanation: A larger population generally produces more births, all else equal.
Births add people to the population stock.
Higher fertility increases the birth flow.
Improved education and family planning tend to reduce fertility, often after social and behavioural delays.
A larger population generally produces more deaths, all else equal.
Deaths remove people from the population stock.
Higher mortality increases the death flow.
Better healthcare access reduces mortality, though health outcomes improve with some delay.
As population rises, available resources per person tend to fall unless total resources grow proportionally.
Higher resources per person can support better access to healthcare over time.
